text:
maria: Alert: a bunch of training pods started failing after last night's node kernel rollout in eu-west1. Error shows CUDA driver/kernel mismatch and NCCL hang in logs.

kevin: seeing same in us-east1 but much smaller. quick log excerpt: `cuda_driver_version: 535.54` vs kernel module expecting `525.*` and `NCCL: NET/ETH CONNECT` timeouts.

maria: stack trace pasted: ```
E tensorflow: cuInit failed: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
NCCL INFO LaunchMode: Group
NCCL WARN Unable to get unique ID (socket connect failed)
```

sre-sam: ng, this looks like the kernel-driver/driver matrix drift we discussed. It was triggered by the automated kernel image roll that bumped to 6.2.x on a subset of pools.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-314 - kernel-driver compatibility regressions. Affected pools: gpu-eu-west-highmem (60 nodes), gpu-us-east-burst (12 nodes).

tina: proposal: immediate hotfix = pin driver + kernel packages on affected pools, and add a lockstep compatibility matrix to prevent auto-roll until validated. Also need an emergency canary rollback for eu-west1.

kevin: agreed. steps I propose: 1) apt-mark hold on the NVIDIA driver package on affected nodes, 2) set kernel package hold (ubuntu-hwe-kernel*) where needed, 3) label nodes as `infra.kernel_pinned=true` so autoscaler/terraform skips them.

sre-sam: commands for quick apply:```bash
# mark driver and kernel as held
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535 
sudo apt-mark hold linux-image-6.2.0-*
# apply apt pin to avoid upgrades via unattended-upgrades
cat > /etc/apt/preferences.d/nvidia-pin <<'EOF'
Package: nvidia-driver-*
Pin: version 535.*
Pin-Priority: 1001
EOF
```
use with care, we'll roll this via salt/ansible.

maria: can we make that less manual? If we label the node pool we can run the automation playbook only for the labeled group. Also add `kubectl label nodes <pool> infra.kernel_pinned=true` for k8s-level routing.

rick: adding the lockstep matrix to the infra repo now. matrix will map: `driver 535 -> cuda 12.2 -> nccl 2.15`, `driver 525 -> cuda 11.8 -> nccl 2.9`. CI preflight will validate that exact combo before admitting a kernel/driver roll.

kevin: we should also add a quick preflight job that runs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv` and the nccl-tests smoke `all_reduce` to catch user-space/BPF/net issues. Example:```bash
# simple preflight smoke
nvidia-smi -q
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-tests.git && make -C nccl-tests/src
./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 1
```
This will capture driver/CUDA/NCCL mismatches early.

tina: operational gating: set a feature flag in the rollout service `infra.upgrades.gate.kernel=true/false`. If false, orchestration will pin images and skip auto-apply. I'll open a PR on the rollout service to consult the gate before scheduling.

sre-sam: monitoring tweak: add alert if `driver_version` drift > 1 minor across nodes in a pool, and a high rate of `NCCL WARN` logs. Also correlate to node reboot counts and KubeOOM events.

maria: capacity/cost note: while we pin, some nodes are unhealthy -> we will shift workloads to dedicated reserved pools (redwood-dedicated-1). That will increase spend ~12% for the short window. ops finance ok with that for 48h.

infra-bot: automation task queued (#3421) to apply apt holds to nodes labeled `kernel-pinned`. ETA: 20m for first wave (canary 3 nodes).

rick: I'll prepare the lockstep JSON map in infra-config repo and add a validator to the upgrade pipeline. Will also add a CLI to query allowed combos.

kevin: temporary rollback plan if hold fails: snapshot node image and redeploy previous kernel image (6.1.x) via nodepool rollback. We should keep rollback scripts handy:```bash
# rollback helper (run from admin bastion)
terraform state pull > tfstate.json
terraform apply -var='node_image=ubuntu-6.1-gpu' -target=module.gpu_nodepool.gpu
```
(not for unsupervised use).

tina: action items: tina -> flip gate to false and coordinate canary rollback; rick -> publish matrix + PR for validator; kevin -> run apt-pin playbook for canary; maria -> monitor incidents and update INC-2026-314.

maria: i'm starting the canary apply now on 3 eu-west1 nodes. will post results in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kevin: thanks. once canary is stable we schedule a controlled rollout by region with 30m observation window.

sre-sam: long term: we need an automated drift detector that blocks kernel auto-rolls when any pool has GPU drivers or NCCL in incompatible set. Also drop a scheduled job to run nccl preflight across all pools nightly.

maria: noted. if canary goes green we'll close INC-2026-314 and convert to a follow-up ticket for the automation work.

infra-bot: canary completed: 3/3 nodes stable. no new NCCL errors in logs (past 15m). Incident severity downgraded to P3.

tina: good job team. I'll run the regional rollout doc and start the PR for the gate.

rick: PR link (draft): https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pulls/458 - includes matrix and validator.

maria: closing loop: update incident with cost estimate, nodes pinned list, and next steps. thanks all. :thumbsup:
